name: Residence
plan: Candidates 1 and 2. (1) A long-term green-card holder gives up the card as a covered expatriate and stays a US resident under the day count; the §877A(a) deemed sale excludes $890,000 of gain and the basis rises by the whole gain. (2) A person below the net-worth and tax tests declines the §877(a)(2)(C) certification to be covered on purpose and takes the same step-up (US realty then sold as a nonresident).
claimed_gain: Plan 1: gain tax $26,180 instead of $238,000 (saves $211,820) with 730/730 US days. Plan 2: $26,180 instead of $200,000 (saves $173,820).

tests.detail: The encoded rule matches §877A(a)(1)-(3), (g)(1)(C), (g)(2)(B), §877(a)(2)(C), (e)(2) word for word and the plan survives the strict re-run, but the figure omits §2801 over the person's lifetime, §877A(d)/(e) acceleration, the prior-year exclusion on a 1 January act, and the immigration precondition.

Denying the exclusion to a person who is a resident for the calendar year after the expatriation year removes plan 1 and leaves the baseline and the leaver unchanged, but plan 2 for a leaver survives it and needs a second edit (no exclusion for a person covered solely under §877(a)(2)(C)).

Removing abandon returns $238,000, removing present leaves no 730-day plan, relocate is decoration, sell is needed only by the search's definition of a finished plan, and present+sell+abandon alone reproduce $26,180.
With the pre-2008 text (no §877A, §877(b) for covered expatriates) no 730-day plan is below $238,000; leavers pay $200,000 on domestic stock or realty, which was the known regime.

No invariant violation in any position reached: gain never created, tax on the gain never above all US tax, one expatriation at most, excluded gain never above the exclusion, ordinary tax of 730-day plans never below 209,994.

23 theorems by decide +kernel replay both plans, the closed-gap results and the earlier law through the full step function, plus bounded universals over every move sequence on the whole-year grid and one unbounded induction (exclusion never exceeded, gain never grows); axioms are propext and Quot.sound only.
A Python script written from the statute text gives the same four figures.

Notice 2009-85 and the 2025 Form 8854 instructions confirm the mechanics; nothing found closes or describes either plan; the 2025 §2801 regulations read resident as domicile, which narrows the (g)(1)(C) switch-off the original relies on; several primary sources were not retrieved.

divergences: §2801 charged only on the giftUS move with a foreign tax home; death and gifts after the 2-year horizon are not counted, though covered status is permanent (§2801(e)(1), (f)): $592,400 on this asset
§877A(g)(1)(C) relief from §2801 is read in Reg. §28.2801-2(b), (h) as residence for chapter 11/12 (domicile), not the §7701(b) day count; the original says staying resident switches §2801 off
§877A(e)(1) deemed distribution of IRAs, HSAs, 529s and §877A(d)(2) acceleration of deferred compensation are not modelled ($175,000 on a $500,000 IRA at 35%)
Expatriation on 1 January puts the deemed sale on 31 December of the prior year: prior-year tax and prior-year exclusion ($866,000 for 2024: $31,892)
One asset: the exclusion is allocated across all gain property and is a single lifetime amount (Notice 2009-85 §3.B); other property of a person covered by the net-worth test is not marked

The abandon move is free and unconditional; §7701(b)(6)(B) needs revocation or an administrative or judicial determination of abandonment, and remaining in the US needs a new immigration status with countable days
Flat rates, no state tax, no growth
Fine 5-segment grid not checked for the green-card scenarios (timed out twice at 175 s)

verdict_reason: The deemed sale, the exclusion and the full basis adjustment are in §877A(a) as encoded and are confirmed by Notice 2009-85 Example 3; no word requires an expatriate to stop being a resident and §877(a)(2)(C) is satisfied by not certifying; ablation, earlier law, kernel replay and independent arithmetic all agree. The claimed gain is a gross ceiling: permanent covered status brings §2801 at 40% on later transfers to US persons made from outside US domicile ($592,400 on this asset, more than the $211,820 or $173,820 saved), so both plans pay only for someone who will die US-domiciled or has no US donees, and plan 1 also needs an immigration status the model does not represent.
